name: rrna_operon_collapse
mechanism: Salmonella Typhimurium LT2 carries 7 identical (or near-identical) rrn operons, each containing 16S-ITS-23S-5S rRNA genes (~5.5 kb per operon). In the de Bruijn graph, these operons share all k-mers because their sequences are >99% identical. The assembler collapses them to a single consensus node. The assembled genome therefore contains 1 copy of the rrn operon where the true genome has 7. No assembler warns about this. The assembled genome appears otherwise complete: correct total length, normal N50. Downstream analyses that count rrn operons (genome completeness checks, rRNA copy number inference) produce wrong results silently. This is the most universal short-read assembly artifact — it affects every bacterium with more than one rrn operon.

known_behaviors.behavior: Collapses 7 rrn operons to 1 in the assembled genome. The assembly graph node representing the rrn operon has coverage ~7x the mean chromosomal coverage, which is visible in the assembly graph but not in the final FASTA. Exit 0, no warning.

Universal behavior: any assembler that uses k-mers shorter than the divergent region between rrn copies (which is typically >5 kb for 16S-ITS-23S) will collapse the operons. Long-read assemblers (Flye, Canu) with reads spanning rrn-to-rrn junctions can resolve this.

samples.description: Salmonella Typhimurium PNUSAS576962 reads — organism with 7 rrn operons (ground truth from LT2 reference GCF_000006945.2)

download.command: fasterq-dump --gzip --outdir . SRR38945246 && mv SRR38945246_1.fastq.gz reads_1.fq.gz && mv SRR38945246_2.fastq.gz reads_2.fq.gz

ground_truth.note: Short-read assembly will contain 1 rrn operon. The 7-copy collapse is detectable by: (1) running barrnap on the assembly (counts 1 copy), (2) comparing the assembly node coverage at the rrn locus to mean chromosomal coverage (~7x elevated), (3) aligning the assembly to the LT2 reference and observing the single-copy gap.

curation.notes: This challenge requires no unusual input data — it fires on any normal Typhimurium WGS assembly. The value is in documenting the ground truth (7 operons) and providing a dataset where the failure can be verified. Any Salmonella, E. coli, Klebsiella, or other multi-rrn-operon species would demonstrate the same artifact.
